fields.name: Nendaz
fields.notes: Domain-wide 4 Vallées figures, shared with Verbier/Veysonnaz/Thyon

fields.name: Veysonnaz
fields.notes: Domain-wide 4 Vallées figures, shared with Verbier/Nendaz/Thyon

fields.name: Thyon
fields.notes: Domain-wide 4 Vallées figures, shared with Verbier/Nendaz/Veysonnaz

fields.name: Champex
fields.notes: Small local area (Champex-Lac); lift co. shared with La Fouly. Season dates not published

fields.name: La Fouly
fields.notes: Small local area (Val Ferret); lift co. shared with Champex

fields.name: Zermatt
fields.notes: Combined Zermatt-Cervinia (Matterhorn Paradise) domain; glacier sector near year-round

fields.name: Saas-Fee
fields.notes: Glacier resort; summer glacier skiing in addition to the main winter season

fields.name: Saas-Grund
fields.notes: Hohsaas area serving Saas-Grund/Saas-Balen

fields.name: Saas-Almagell
fields.notes: Small local Heidbodme area; operating company name unconfirmed

fields.name: Leukerbad
fields.notes: Torrent-Bahnen area; separate Gemmi-Bahnen AG runs the Gemmi cable car

fields.name: Grimentz
fields.notes: Shared combined Grimentz-Zinal ski area

fields.name: Zinal
fields.notes: Shared combined Grimentz-Zinal ski area

fields.name: Vercorin
fields.notes: Independent area, not lift-connected to Grimentz-Zinal

fields.name: St-Luc
fields.notes: Shared St-Luc/Chandolin domain; figures are domain-wide

fields.name: Chandolin
fields.notes: Shared St-Luc/Chandolin domain; figures domain-wide, base = Chandolin village 1936 m

fields.name: Arolla
fields.notes: Espace Dent-Blanche is a shared PASS, not a connected domain; figures are Arolla only

fields.name: Les Haudères
fields.notes: Only lift is the Homazo baby lift; the real nearby area is La Forclaz/La Sage

fields.name: Evolène
fields.notes: Lannaz-Chemeuille sector of Espace Dent-Blanche; not lift-connected to Arolla

fields.name: Riederalp
fields.notes: Sector of the connected Aletsch Arena domain; run count not published by operator

fields.name: Bettmeralp
fields.notes: Sector of the connected Aletsch Arena domain; run count not published by operator

fields.name: Fiescheralp
fields.notes: Sector of the connected Aletsch Arena domain; Eggishorn cableway starts here

fields.name: Reckingen
fields.notes: Village beginner lift (stands at Gluringen); season dates not published. Goms is mainly cross-country

fields.name: Münster
fields.notes: Small beginner/family area with lifts at Münster and Geschinen

fields.name: Obergoms
fields.notes: Municipality (Oberwald/Obergesteln/Ulrichen); only the village Skilift Oberwald. Hungerberg closed 2009

fields.name: Champéry
fields.notes: Domain-wide Portes du Soleil (CH+FR) figures; local Planachaux sector tops ~2277 m

fields.name: Morgins
fields.notes: Domain-wide Portes du Soleil figures; local La Foilleuse sector tops ~2000 m

fields.name: Torgon
fields.notes: Domain-wide Portes du Soleil figures; Torgon sector is small (~4 lifts). Télé-Torgon SA went bankrupt, lifts bought by SETT Jan 2025

fields.name: Val d'Entremont
fields.notes: Vichères-Liddes is the only lift-served area in Val d'Entremont; Grand-St-Bernard pass has none

fields.name: St. Moritz
fields.notes: Corviglia-Marguns-Piz Nair sector; village 1822 m, lift base 1772 m

fields.name: Pontresina
fields.notes: Pontresina village (1805 m) has no area of its own; its skiing is Diavolezza + Lagalb in Val Bernina

fields.name: Sils-Maria
fields.notes: Village on the shared Corvatsch/Furtschellas domain; Furtschellas cable car departs Sils

fields.name: Silvaplana
fields.notes: Shared Corvatsch/Furtschellas domain; lift base at Surlej 1870 m

fields.name: Celerina
fields.notes: Own lift into the Corviglia/Marguns domain shared with St. Moritz

fields.name: Corvatsch
fields.notes: Corvatsch (Silvaplana-Surlej) run as one domain with Furtschellas; 3303 m is the highest lift point in Graubünden

fields.name: Diavolezza
fields.notes: Diavolezza sector only; piste km not published per sector (Diavolezza+Lagalb combined = 35 km / 5 lifts)

fields.name: Zuoz
fields.notes: Small local Pizzet/Albanas area, unconnected. Zuoz is Upper, not Lower, Engadin

fields.name: La Punt
fields.notes: Not a resort: one 1 km beginner slope, 2 practice lifts. Roughly mid-Dec to mid-Mar; dates not published

fields.name: Scuol
fields.notes: Motta Naluns; access from Scuol, Ftan and Sent. Some sources quote 80 km incl. valley runs

fields.name: Ftan
fields.notes: Village on the Motta Naluns domain via the Ftan-Prui chairlift

fields.name: Samnaun
fields.notes: Swiss side of the cross-border Silvretta Arena Samnaun/Ischgl; figures are the whole binational domain

fields.name: Münstertal
fields.notes: Minschuns area above Tschierv; lift base Alp da Munt 2150 m, valley villages 1250-1660 m

fields.name: Santa Maria VM
fields.notes: Village (1386 m) with no lifts of its own; figures are the shared Minschuns area

fields.name: Poschiavo
fields.notes: Valley town (~1014 m) with only a small children's tow at Viale; no marked ski area

fields.name: Bergell
fields.notes: Val Bregaglia is mostly touring; only lift-served skiing is the Sur Cresta tow at Casaccia

fields.name: Maloja
fields.notes: Small Aela T-bar plus pony lift. Operator announced Aela stays closed for winter 2026/27 for maintenance

fields.name: Davos
fields.notes: Operator figures for the whole Davos Klosters network (Parsenn, Jakobshorn, Rinerhorn, Pischa, Schatzalp, Madrisa)

fields.name: Klosters
fields.notes: Same network/pass as Davos; Klosters' own mountains are Madrisa (26 km, 9 lifts) and Gotschna

fields.name: Parsenn
fields.notes: Sector, not a standalone resort. Base 810 m is Küblis, foot of the 12 km Weissfluhgipfel-Küblis run

fields.name: Arosa
fields.notes: Arosa sector only; linked to Lenzerheide by the Urdenbahn (combined domain 225 km / 43 lifts)

fields.name: Lenzerheide
fields.notes: Lenzerheide sector (includes Churwalden lifts); combined Arosa Lenzerheide domain 225 km / 43 lifts

fields.name: Churwalden
fields.notes: Churwalden (1229 m) is the lowest base of the Lenzerheide domain

fields.name: Flims
fields.notes: Village of the connected Flims Laax Falera domain; figures are domain-wide

fields.name: Laax
fields.notes: Village of the connected Flims Laax Falera domain; other databases quote 224 km / 28 lifts

fields.name: Falera
fields.notes: Village of the connected Flims Laax Falera domain; Falera village sits at ~1220 m

fields.name: Disentis
fields.notes: Disentis 3000; daily operation from ~12-20. Separate, unconnected domain from Sedrun

fields.name: Obersaxen
fields.notes: Obersaxen Mundaun Val Lumnezia; Graubünden Tourism quotes 117 km, operator ~120 km

fields.name: Safiental
fields.notes: Only lift-served skiing in Safiental is the single Tenna solar ski lift; rest of the valley is touring

fields.name: Vals
fields.notes: Vals-Dachberg; gondola Vals-Gadastatt plus drag lifts

fields.name: Splügen
fields.notes: Largest area in the Viamala/Rheinwald region. Graubünden Tourism quotes 6 lifts / 33 km

fields.name: Bivio
fields.notes: Small independent area; official site claims 30+ km, databases give 27 km. Weekend-only in early Dec

fields.name: Avers
fields.notes: Very small high-altitude area at Avers-Juppa; mostly steep/ungroomed. Run count not published

fields.name: Savognin
fields.notes: Full resort in Surses/Parc Ela; skiresort.info gives 73.5 km / base 1168 m

fields.name: Bergün
fields.notes: Darlux plus village beginner lifts; partly weekend/holiday operation. Also the 6 km Preda-Bergün sledge run

fields.name: Grindelwald
fields.notes: Shares the Kleine Scheidegg/Männlichen domain with Wengen. Grindelwald-First is a separate area, not included

fields.name: Wengen
fields.notes: Same shared domain as Grindelwald; base given is Wengen village (domain low point is 1034 m)

fields.name: Mürren
fields.notes: Separate Mürren-Schilthorn domain, NOT lift-connected to Kleine Scheidegg. Base 796 m is Lauterbrunnen station; village 1638 m

fields.name: Gstaad
fields.notes: Shared Gstaad region (one pass, 9 sectors, not all lift-connected). Top 3016 m is Glacier 3000

fields.name: Saanen
fields.notes: Shared Gstaad region figures; Saanen's local sector is Eggli / La Videmanette (58 km, 9 lifts)

fields.name: Schönried
fields.notes: Shared Gstaad region figures; Schönried's local sectors are Horneggli and Rellerli

fields.name: Zweisimmen
fields.notes: Rinderberg/Saanerslochgrat/Horneggli sector serving Zweisimmen/Saanenmöser/Schönried/St. Stephan

fields.name: Lenk
fields.notes: Betelberg sector; former Lenk Bergbahnen merged into Bergbahnen Adelboden-Lenk AG in 2023/24

fields.name: Adelboden
fields.notes: Chuenisbärgli/Silleren/Hahnenmoos/Metsch sector, incl. the Chuenisbärgli World Cup slope

fields.name: Kandersteg
fields.notes: Oeschinensee sector; small standalone area, not part of a larger domain

fields.name: Meiringen
fields.notes: Shared domain with Hasliberg; Meiringen town (~595 m) connects via gondola

fields.name: Hasliberg
fields.notes: Same connected Meiringen-Hasliberg domain

fields.name: Grimmialp
fields.notes: Small family area in the Diemtigtal nature park, near Schwenden

fields.name: Frutigen
fields.notes: Elsigen-Metsch sector; accessed from Achseten near Frutigen, not from the town itself

fields.name: Beatenberg
fields.notes: Small Niederhorn family area above Beatenberg

fields.name: Lötschental
fields.notes: Valley of several villages; the Lauchernalp domain is accessed by cable car from Wiler

fields.name: Leysin
fields.notes: Leysin sector; bus-linked to Les Mosses-La Lécherette for a combined ~100 km
fields.operator_name: Télé Leysin-Col des Mosses-La Lécherette SA (TLML)

fields.name: Villars-sur-Ollon
fields.notes: Connected Villars-Gryon-Les Diablerets domain; TVGD markets 100+ km, measured 87 km

fields.name: Gryon
fields.notes: Gryon village 1130 m, gondola base at Barboleuse; figures are the whole connected domain

fields.name: Les Diablerets
fields.notes: Village 1160 m, joins the domain via Meilleret. The local Isenau sector has been closed since 2017/18

fields.name: Glacier 3000
fields.notes: Distinct glacier area, separate operator from TVGD. Base = Col du Pillon station; lowest lift point Reusch ~1345 m

fields.name: Moléson
fields.notes: Fribourg pre-alpine area; funicular to Plan-Francey plus cable car to the 2002 m summit. Short low-altitude season

fields.name: Charmey
fields.notes: Charmey-Vounetz; run count not published, lift count varies 4-5 by source

fields.name: Jaun
fields.notes: Small area at the foot of the Gastlosen; run count not reliably published

fields.name: Rochers-de-Naye
fields.notes: Still operating: ~1 km of piste, rail access only via the MOB cog railway. Lift count varies 3-5 by source

fields.name: Andermatt
fields.notes: SkiArena Andermatt-Sedrun. With Disentis the combined region is 180 km / 33 lifts. Majority-owned by Vail Resorts since 2022

fields.name: Realp
fields.notes: Small T-bar + pony lift at the foot of the Furka Pass; separate from SkiArena, limited weekday opening

fields.name: Engelberg
fields.notes: Covers Titlis-Trübsee-Jochpass plus the separate Brunni sector; Titlis sector alone is ~70 km / 18 lifts. Glacier gives a long season

fields.name: Melchsee-Frutt
fields.notes: Base is Stöckalp 1080 m; the car-free village sits at ~1920 m, reached by gondola

fields.name: Elm
fields.notes: Elm im Sernftal; official site states 40 km (some aggregators say 44), lift count varies 5-6

fields.name: Wildhaus
fields.notes: Wildhaus-Gamserrugg sector. Shares the Toggenburg pass with Chäserrugg but is NOT lift-connected to it

fields.name: Unterwasser
fields.notes: Base village of the Chäserrugg/Unterwasser/Alt St. Johann sector; different operator from Wildhaus, not lift-connected

fields.name: Flumserberg
fields.notes: Largest area between Zurich and Chur. Gondola also runs from Unterterzen (425 m); lowest piste ends at 665 m

fields.name: Pizol
fields.notes: Base 509 m is the Bad Ragaz valley station; second base at Wangs. Resort markets ~50 km incl. ski routes

fields.name: Airolo
fields.notes: Airolo-Pesciüm, Valle Leventina. Plus ~10 km of ski routes and ~1 km night skiing. Run count not published

fields.name: Bedretto
fields.notes: Cioss Prato (Villa, Bedretto): one T-bar plus a children's lift, 60 m vertical. Val Bedretto is mainly cross-country

fields.name: Bosco Gurin
fields.notes: Grossalp above Bosco/Gurin, Ticino's highest and only Walser-German village. Some sources quote ~2400 m top

fields.name: Blenio
fields.notes: Matched to Campo Blenio. Lucomagno pass itself has no lifts. Nara-Leontica is in Acquarossa, not Blenio
fields.operator_name: Società Cooperativa Impianti Turistici Campo Blenio-Ghirone

fields.name: San Bernardino
fields.notes: Closed for several years, reopened 27 Dec 2023 under new owner. Operation remains snow/finance dependent - verify each season

fields.name: Bernina Pass
fields.notes: road/rail pass (2328 m); the lift areas nearby are Diavolezza and Lagalb

fields.name: Binntal
fields.notes: nature park valley; only a ~300 m village drag lift at Binn

fields.name: Blatten
fields.notes: no lifts of its own (valley skiing is via Lauchernalp from Wiler); village largely destroyed by the May 2025 rockslide

fields.name: Conters
fields.notes: small village, no lifts; nearest are Pany-Luzein and Grüsch Danusa

fields.name: Grimsel
fields.notes: mountain pass road under winter closure; no lifts

fields.name: Génépy
fields.notes: no lift-served area under this name; high alpine terrain

fields.name: Haut Val de Bagnes
fields.notes: hiking valley with dam (Mauvoisin), no lifts

fields.name: Klausenpass
fields.notes: road pass (1948 m) closed from late Oct/early Nov to late May/June; no lifts

fields.name: Mattmark
fields.notes: reservoir and dam above Saas-Almagell, road closed in winter

fields.name: Monte Rosa
fields.notes: glacier/massif above Zermatt, touring terrain; lift access via Zermatt Bergbahnen

fields.name: Mountet
fields.notes: Cabane du Grand Mountet, SAC mountaineering hut at 2886 m

fields.name: Schams
fields.notes: no operating lift area (Zillis-Schamserberg defunct); sledging and winter hiking only

fields.name: Sustenpass
fields.notes: mountain pass road under winter closure; no lifts

fields.name: Turtmann
fields.notes: side valley; the Turtmann-Unterems-Oberems cableway is public transport, no pistes

fields.name: Val Chamuera
fields.notes: side valley above La Punt/Madulain, ski touring only

fields.name: Val S-charl
fields.notes: quiet side valley south of Scuol, touring and snowshoeing only

fields.name: Val Suot
fields.notes: side valley in the Scuol/Zernez area, touring terrain only

fields.name: Val dal Spöl
fields.notes: inside Swiss National Park; skiing and off-path travel prohibited

fields.name: Zervreila
fields.notes: reservoir and hamlet at the head of the Valsertal; nearest lifts are Vals-Dachberg

fields.name: oberes Puschlav
fields.notes: upper Val Poschiavo/Bernina area; touring and cross-country only, Livigno's lifts are in Italy

fields.name: westl. Silvretta
fields.notes: regional ski-touring / avalanche-bulletin label, not a resort

fields.name: östliche Silvretta
fields.notes: regional touring/avalanche-bulletin label, not a lift-served area

fields.name: Sedrun
fields.why_it_matters: Graubünden half of SkiArena Andermatt-Sedrun. Sheet already carries Andermatt at 120 km domain figures with no Sedrun row.

fields.name: Anzère
fields.why_it_matters: Open bowls under Pas de Maimbré; main gateway to Wildhorn/Rawil touring.

fields.name: Hoch-Ybrig
fields.why_it_matters: Largest resort in Schwyz, heavy Zurich day-trip load, busy touring hub (Druesberg, Fluebrig).

fields.name: Mythenregion
fields.why_it_matters: Ibergeregg and the Mythen flanks are among the busiest touring areas in Central CH, with a real accident record.

fields.name: Grächen
fields.why_it_matters: Largest Valais resort absent. Seetalhorn high alpine terrain, heavy off-piste.

fields.name: Sörenberg
fields.why_it_matters: Largest resort in Lucerne, only high-alpine terrain in the Entlebuch. Brienzer Rothorn freeride.

fields.name: Klewenalp-Stockhütte
fields.why_it_matters: Main lift-served area in Nidwalden; north-facing bowls under Brisen.

fields.name: Brigels/Waltensburg/Andiast
fields.why_it_matters: Mid-size Surselva area, known powder descents toward Waltensburg.

fields.name: Les Mosses-La Lécherette
fields.why_it_matters: One of Romandie's busiest touring basins (Pic Chaussy, Para) with frequent involvements.

fields.name: Blatten-Belalp
fields.why_it_matters: 1796 m vertical to 3118 m; strong freeride reputation, marked ski routes.

fields.name: Stoos
fields.why_it_matters: Fronalpstock and Klingenstock are steep and exposed; terrain quality exceeds lift count.

fields.name: Nax - Mont-Noble
fields.why_it_matters: Reaches 2640 m at the mouth of Val d'Hérens; popular randonnée circuits.

fields.name: Tschiertschen
fields.why_it_matters: Nationally known freeride destination. Four lifts, disproportionate avalanche relevance.

fields.name: Grüsch Danusa
fields.why_it_matters: Mid-size Prättigau area with substantial off-piste and a touring gateway.

fields.name: Chur Brambrüesch
fields.why_it_matters: Cable car from the city; common Dreibündenstein touring start.

fields.name: Schwarzsee
fields.why_it_matters: Fribourg's most important touring hub (Kaiseregg, Schafberg); high accident density for its altitude.

fields.name: Carì
fields.why_it_matters: Mid-size Leventina area; touring base for the Campolungo group.

fields.name: Bellwald
fields.why_it_matters: Goms sun terrace to 2558 m; common start for Goms tours.

fields.name: Rougemont - La Videmanette
fields.why_it_matters: Vaud gateway into the Gstaad domain; Gummfluh couloirs.

fields.name: Sarn (Heinzenberg)
fields.why_it_matters: Natural-snow slopes, touring toward Bischolapass.

fields.name: Hochwang
fields.why_it_matters: Natural-snow Schanfigg area, notable touring hill.

fields.name: Unterbäch
fields.why_it_matters: Adjoins Moosalp/Eischoll; Ginals terrain to 2443 m.

fields.name: Amden-Arvenbüel
fields.why_it_matters: Mattstock and the Amden terraces; steep sun-exposed south faces.

fields.name: Engstligenalp
fields.why_it_matters: High plateau above Adelboden, own cable car, not piste-connected. Primary Wildstrubel touring launch.

fields.name: Fideriser Heuberge
fields.why_it_matters: Car-free, tour-focused clientele. High open avalanche-prone terrain (Arflina, Chüpfenflue).

fields.name: Axalp ob Brienz
fields.why_it_matters: Natural-snow slopes; touring toward Windegg.

fields.name: Alt St. Johann - Sellamatt
fields.why_it_matters: Separate Toggenburg base under the Churfirsten north faces — a frequently fatal touring zone.

fields.name: Mörlialp
fields.why_it_matters: Main non-Melchsee area in Obwalden; open bowls toward Glaubenbielen.

fields.name: Wiriehorn
fields.why_it_matters: Diemtigtal; steep north flanks. Sheet already has Grimmialp in the same valley.

fields.name: Säntis - Schwägalp
fields.why_it_matters: No groomed pistes — pure freeride/ski-route terrain. Operator suspends skier transport from level 3 up.

fields.name: Ebenalp - Wasserauen
fields.why_it_matters: Principal winter access into the Alpstein; standard start for heavily used tours.

fields.name: Brunni - Engelberg
fields.why_it_matters: Separate operator opposite Titlis; Ristis/Rigidalstock touring start.

fields.name: Gitschenen - Isenthal
fields.why_it_matters: Two lifts, nationally known touring base (Uri Rotstock, Schwalmis, Brisen).

fields.name: St. Antönien
fields.why_it_matters: Tiny village lift. One of Switzerland's most important touring basins, very high backcountry traffic.

fields.name: Bannalp
fields.why_it_matters: High snow-sure plateau; touring base for Walenstöcke, Ruchstock, Brisen.

fields.name: Lauenen
fields.why_it_matters: Single lift, but a heavily used touring valley (Wildhorn, Geltenhorn).

fields.name: Brunni - Alpthal
fields.why_it_matters: One lift. Among the most used touring and snowshoe trailheads in Central CH, significant accident record.

fields.name: Haldigrat
fields.why_it_matters: Freeride-only, no prepared pistes, no avalanche control on the descents. A pure decision venue.
